candidates.blocker: 2026-06-21 threshold refresh plus family low-water-context recheck. This Noblesville family still has one of the cleaner Indiana access packages, but it is not implementation-ready. Official Hamilton County and Noblesville pages still support Potter's Bridge Park canoe launch and the Forest Park White River Boat Ramp as real public endpoints, and Discover White River's current paddling page explicitly lists Potter's Bridge Park and Forest Park among the popular put-in and takeout points for the Noblesville section. IndianaOutfitters still preserves a nearby Hoosier Canoe Club report of a nice/swift Perkinsville-to-Noblesville trip at 430 cfs on gauge 03349000, and Hoosier Canoe Club's April 26 2026 Potter's Bridge-to-116th Street newsletter report says the family still had a line through low water at about 3.65 ft on the 146th Street gauge. That is better family-level low-water context than the earlier operator fallback alone, but it still does not create a source-backed low-water floor or exact route-specific scoring model for Potter's Bridge-to-Forest Park on gauge 03349000. Keep the lead blocked on missing exact-route minimums and unresolved low-head-dam/private-bank handling around Clare and downstream Noblesville.

Sangamon River Alliance's current site still preserves the exact USRC Hazen Bridge to Lake of the Woods float-trip write-up, including the named route, 5.5-mile distance, and Fisher gauge guidance: 4.5 ft was lower than recommended, 5.5 to 6 ft is better for enjoyment, and the trip should stay below about 10 ft flood stage. That was enough to prove the old Lincoln Heritage family contains one real exact upper-Sangamon subreach. Until current manager-grade sources confirm the completed launch/take-out arrangement and public paddler use, this narrowed Hazen-to-Lake-of-the-Woods lead is parked as blocked_until_date rather than left in active access churn.
